findings.title: The plan builds a new coverage matrix although a live-vs-disk reconciliation already exists and is already rendered
findings.quote: - **Coverage** is inferred from counts + export progress; there is no per-area reconciliation
findings.claim: verify.py already computes per-area {live, exported, missing} plus the missing id list, and worker-pool persists it as account.verify; OverviewTab already renders that matrix with live/exported/missing and a 'complete' badge. P0-2's stated reason (nothing reconciles) is false, so the plan adds a second, manifest-derived truth beside a working one.
findings.impact: Two 'missing' numbers for the same account. The existing Verify panel says live 104 / exported 104 / complete; the new matrix counts 124 files on disk and reports 20 photos that are not missing. The operator cannot tell which one to act on the console's central question.

findings.fix: P0-2 should render and extend account.verify.areas (live, exported, missing + verify.missing ids) instead of recomputing coverage. Add 'bytes' and 'last export' from account.export, and label the columns 'last verified <timeAgo>'.

findings.title: Two code paths write different photos/hidden counts for the same export: 104/9 from the manifest, 124/18 from disk
findings.claim: The worker's collect_counts derives photos/hidden from manifest rows with status='done' (104 photos, 9 hidden for export/example.harvest@icloud.com), while countsFromExport walks the tree (124, 18). The 20 library and 9 hidden '.HEIC.mp4' live-photo proxies have no manifest row, so the two definitions differ by 29 files by construction. Which number the panel shows depends on which branch last wrote.
findings.impact: Overview 'Photos' reads 104 after a worker export with counts, or 124 after any Node fallback/repair, while the gallery lists 124+18 tiles. P0-2's acceptance 'Matrix equals manifest.sqlite3 summary and file counts' can never pass for the account it names, and a downloaded>live row will show exported 124 vs live 104.

findings.title: account.counts is the export tree, not live iCloud; the matrix's 'live count' column will equal 'downloaded' and missing will read 0
findings.quote: | P0-2 | **Coverage matrix** per account: area × (live count, downloaded, missing, bytes, last export); totals reconcile with manifest and disk |
findings.claim: export_done overwrites account.counts with disk totals ('The export knows what is actually on disk, so its counts replace the old numbers'), and export-counts.js states the panel's Counts must describe the export. The cited acceptance account example.harvest has verify:null and counts {photos:124,hidden:18} — pure disk numbers. Sourcing 'live' from counts makes live == downloaded and missing == 0 for every account that has exported.
findings.impact: The matrix answers 'what is missing' with 0 for exactly the accounts an operator inspects, and never shows the new iCloud photos that are the reason to look. It fails in the optimistic direction, so nobody notices.

findings.title: A restart strands every running job as 'unknown' before the pool boots; the pool's requeue branch can never fire
findings.claim: Store.markStaleJobs runs in the constructor (store.js:130) and rewrites running/twofa to 'unknown'. WorkerPool is built afterwards (socket/index.js:35) and rebuilds the queue only from 'queued' and 'running' (worker-pool.js:144-156), so the 'running' branch is dead code and no path ever requeues 'unknown'. ACTIVE_JOB also excludes 'unknown', so the account looks recoverable while the job is terminal.
findings.impact: After a deploy, an in-flight sign-in or export shows 'unknown — node restarted' forever; the visitor's tab gets no result, the export is silently restarted from scratch, and P0-3's 'order persists after restart' is false for the only jobs that matter.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'job.status = "unknown"' server/store.js; sed -n '144,156p' server/socket/worker-pool.js; sed -n '129,131p' server/store.js
findings.fix: Requeue on a set that includes 'unknown' (or move stale-marking into WorkerPool, after the store is loaded), and add a test that constructs a Store over a file with a running job and then asserts pool.queue contains it.

findings.title: flush() deletes jobs from the live map past 1000, including still-queued ones, and pump() silently drops their ids
findings.claim: Every debounced save reassigns this.jobs to the newest 1000 jobs by createdAt. Jobs load from disk (up to 1000) and new ones are added, so a queued job older than 1000 newer ones is evicted while pool.queue still holds its id; pump() then sees getJob()==undefined and splices it. With tied createdAt values the eviction is arbitrary, not oldest-first: a probe of 1005 creates in one tick evicted 5 jobs starting at index 70.
findings.impact: An account sits at 'exporting 0/0' with no job row, no error and no done event — the exact invisible failure P0-1 promises to fix, reached by a 500-account campaign (FEATURES:95) or by one bulk enqueue.
findings.fix: Cap only terminal jobs (done/error/invalid/cancelled/unknown) and never evict anything in queued/running; build a new map instead of truncating the live one, and assert a queued job survives 1000 later creations.

findings.title: updateAccount's allowlist silently discards priority/order/note, so P0-3's 'state survives reload' fails with no error
findings.claim: Only the 16 listed scalar keys and 9 object keys are merged; defaultAccount declares no priority/order/note. updateAccount({priority,order,note}) returns a normal account with all three absent — confirmed by probe — so a client or socket handler that writes priority believes it succeeded.
findings.impact: P0-3's acceptance 'order persists after restart' and the priority badge silently do nothing; the operator re-pins 500 accounts and after a reload every pin is gone, with no error to explain it.
findings.fix: Add priority/order/note to defaultAccount and to the scalar allowlist, and make updateAccount reject or report unknown keys instead of returning success.

findings.title: '3 selected accounts produce 3 ordered jobs' cannot hold: front-insert is LIFO and the boot queue re-sorts by rank, not operator order
findings.claim: startExport passes priority into enqueue(id, front=true), which unshifts each job, so selecting A,B,C dispatches C,B,A. After a restart the queue is rebuilt and sorted by rank -> notesMissing -> createdAt, with no operator order at all, so even persisted priority would not survive.
findings.impact: The operator's chosen order is reversed in a live session and lost across a deploy, while the screenshot acceptance test ('3 ordered jobs') passes if nobody checks the order direction.
findings.fix: Give jobs an explicit order field and insert by it (or enqueue bulk in reverse); include it as the first sort key in the boot rebuild.

findings.title: P1-1's premise is wrong on the export it cites: 20 of 142 tiles are .mp4 and the Photo kind returns zero items
findings.quote: 142/142 tiles are `.mp4` proxies; "Photo" filter gives the same set
findings.claim: export/example.harvest@icloud.com holds 124 Library files (93 PNG, 20 jpg, 11 mp4) and 18 Hidden (9 jpg, 9 mp4) — 20 videos, 122 stills. gallery() derives kind from Scan/vlm-index.json, which does not exist in any export tree here, so kindCounts is {unclassified:142} and kind='photo' returns total 0, not 'the same proxies'. The 'paged gallery' in FEATURES:53 is also false: PhotosTab sends pageSize=PAGE_SIZE=0, which export.js treats as 'everything in one response'.
findings.impact: The P1 item is scoped to hide 20 live-photo proxies, not 142 tiles, and its acceptance ('default gallery contains no .mp4 tiles') passes without implementing the still+proxy grouping it promises. The real defect — kind is an optional VLM label, so the filter is empty by default — survives untouched.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'PAGE_SIZE = 0' src/admin/PhotosTab.jsx; sed -n '346,349p' server/admin/export.js; ls export/example.harvest@icloud.com/Photos/Library | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c
findings.fix: Specify images-only as 'item.video === false' (a real field) rather than kind='photo'; make the kind filter fall back to a media-type label when vlm-index.json is absent; and state in the acceptance that a live-photo still and its .mp4 count as one tile.

findings.title: The cancelled-job guard in handleError is dead code, so a cancelled wave export is recorded as failed and counted as wave-done
findings.claim: Line 1158 assigns status 'error' to the same object before this test, so job.status is always 'error' and the guard never matches. A wave-replaced job that then errors sets the account to 'error' and falls through to onWaveJobDone, marking the account done for the wave. Cancellation is also not an abort: the exporter keeps enumerating remaining phases and always emits job:export_done with partial totals.
findings.impact: P0-1's 'cancel' either reports failure after cancelling or lets a replaced export count as finished, so a wave advances on work that did not happen. Retry/cancel semantics cannot be built on this path unchanged.
findings.fix: Capture the pre-patch status before updateJob (or test job.status against a saved value) and return early; have the exporter emit a distinct cancelled event so Node can distinguish cancel from failure.

findings.title: P0-1's acceptance names a 'failed' job state that does not exist, and no test asserts the claims the plan rests on
findings.quote: Mock-worker run leaves ≥1 job in each of queued/running/done/failed
findings.claim: Job statuses written by the code are queued, running, twofa, done, error, invalid, unknown, cancelled — there is no 'failed'. Separately, the suite asserts the stale-job defect as intent (store.test: 'running jobs are marked unknown') and nothing asserts a pool requeue, pageSize<=0 (the client's only gallery path), the gallery kind filter, or priority persistence; library.test exercises the wave scheduler through Object.create(WorkerPool.prototype), so the constructor's boot rebuild is never run.
findings.impact: The acceptance test is unwritable as phrased, and the restart, paging, kind-filter and priority behaviours the plan changes have no regression cover, so each can ship broken while the suite stays green.
findings.verification_command: grep -rn 'failed' server/store.js | head; sed -n '39,40p' server/test/store.test.mjs; grep -n 'Object.create(WorkerPool.prototype)' server/test/library.test.mjs
findings.fix: Use the real status vocabulary in the acceptance (queued/running/done/error), and add four tests: boot requeue over a reloaded store, gallery pageSize=0, kind filter with and without vlm-index.json, and account priority round-trip.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: The socket process restarts while an export job is running; the plan assumes the job resumes (P0-3 'order persists after restart').
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: Executed probe: Store over a file with one running export -> reload -> job.status='unknown', account.status='connected'; new WorkerPool -> pool.queue=[] and activeJobForAccount('export')=null. Cause: store.js:130 markStaleJobs runs in the constructor before socket/index.js:35 builds the pool.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: A job set to 'running' between store load and pool construction would still hit the branch; no code path does that.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: P0-3 stores per-account priority/order/note and reloads the dashboard.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: Probe: updateAccount(id, {priority:7, order:2, note:'call back'}) then read back -> {} (all three undefined). store.js:398-423 is an allowlist; defaultAccount (store.js:50-118) declares none of them.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: Unless the implementer edits both defaultAccount and the allowlist, in which case the field persists but nothing consumes it.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: P0-2 acceptance: 'Matrix equals manifest.sqlite3 summary and file counts for example.harvest'.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: Manifest summary and on-disk counts agree for that account.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: manifest.sqlite3 status='done' -> photos 104 / hidden 9; disk -> Library 124 / Hidden 18; countsFromExport -> {photos:124, hidden:18, videos:20, images:104}; exporter.collect_counts -> 104/9. Difference is the 29 live-photo .mp4 proxies, which have no manifest row.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: 'File counts' could be redefined to count only manifest-backed assets, but then the gallery column (142 files) still disagrees.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: The gallery 'Photo' kind selects the same set as 'Any type' (FEATURES:53,102).
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: gallery() on the cited export: kind='photo' -> total 0, items 0; kind='' -> 142 items, 20 video, kindCounts={'unclassified':142}. No vlm-index.json exists in any export tree in the repo.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: The tour screenshot (17-photos-kind-photo.png) shows 142 mp4 tiles that do not exist in the cited export, so its fixture is unknown; a tree with a vlm-index could behave differently.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Node cannot read manifest.sqlite3 because there is no SQLite dependency (map.md claim, and P0-2's implied blocker).
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: Only Python can open the manifest.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: server/gate.js:23-26 loads node:sqlite via createRequire; node -v is v24.21.0. Nothing yet reads the manifest from Node.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: node:sqlite is experimental and needs Node >= 22.5; package.json has no engines field, so a production Node below that throws at require.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: A cancelled export stops and the account returns to a clean state.
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: job:cancel aborts the exporter; handleError's cancelled guard protects the account.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: exporter.py checks ctx.cancel only inside _drain() and a few loops, then run() continues to the next phase's enumerate_* and always emits job:export_done (exporter.py:1059). In Node, worker-pool.js:1158 overwrites status before the 1193 guard, so the guard never fires.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: Cancel does stop further downloads within one drain, so no corruption, only continued enumeration and a partial 'done'.

open_questions: Which number is the operator's source of truth for 'photos': iCloud assets (104) or files on disk (142)? P0-2 and P0-4 need one answer before either is coded.
Where did the tour screenshot's 142 '.mp4' tree (IMG_0249.mp4 etc.) come from? No such files exist under export/, so the screenshot does not prove the real export rendering it is cited for.
Is a Socket.IO process restarted by the deploy while workers keep running? If so, the unknown-job stranding also loses the worker-side result for a job the node forgot.
Is node:sqlite guaranteed in deployment (Node >= 22.5)? A manifest reader on an older Node fails at require, not at query.

If Node reads the manifest while the Python exporter holds it with commit-per-row and no WAL, does a DatabaseSync read return SQLITE_BUSY? gate.js sets busy_timeout on its own DB; a manifest reader would need the same.
Do more than 1000 jobs accrue in one process lifetime in real use? The demo store has 125; a 500-account campaign is ~2500-4000.
